prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: hospital dispensing/returns; authorized, traceable custody. Aliases: Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Items produced: Morrowglass—Order Reconciliation Snapshot; Clinical Pharmacist—Dose Exception Review Slip; Copperfield—Cold Chain Handoff Card; Cinderwake—Priority Refill Tote Tag; Juniper—Batch Release Note; Hospital Courier—Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record; East Tube Dispatch Console—Tube Route Exception Ticket; Charge Nurse—Cabinet Downtime Notice; Medication Safety Officer—Diversion Review Packet; Tallowmere—Return Bin. Morrowglass validates/routes/statuses orders; holds unresolved/canceled/duplicate/superseded orders; rejects incomplete/inconsistent updates, retaining reasons. Release requires order/instruction/product/destination agreement, identifiers/time/credentials. Copperfield verifies contents/packaging/lot/expiry/cold-chain, reverifies delays; gathers evidence, never decides clinical doses. Cinderwake prepares authorized orders; exceptions stop picks, preserve scans/quantities, hold packages. Juniper compares active order/product/strength/measured quantity; blocks differences; slip records category/evidence/disposition/reviewer. Exceptions include mismatch/omission/duplicate/clinical implausibility; authorized disposition required. Clinical Pharmacist assesses dose/route/timing/patient concerns; corrections require authorized orders, never history inference. Larkspur locks transactions, confirms nonadministration, escalates urgent concerns; never bypasses/substitutes. Bluejay logs/displays temperatures/excursion extent-duration/connectivity-loss; affected stock unavailable pending assessment; refrigerate until transfer. Courier verifies/records custody; collects only closed, ready-recorded bins. Reconcile manifests before Pneumatic Tube Network admission; East checks/logs routes; West Tube Dispatch Console controls authorized routing. Hold faults; document resolution; alternatives retain custody; restoration requires authorized checks. Receiving staff verify identifiers/destination/count/condition; isolate discrepancies, stage pending authorization. North Ward Cabinet Controller uses tote tag; both it and South Ward Cabinet Controller record arrival/destination, block Out of Service; Ready for Dispense requires checks. North blocks holds; South reports lock/access failures. Stonewake repairs/verifies; IT Operations Specialist checks interfaces/connectivity/health. Returns: reconcile before

New part:
S140: The Medication Safety Officer reviews suspected diversion, repeated high-risk exceptions, and events with potential for patient harm.
S141: IT Operations Specialist receives the Diversion Review Packet and checks access, transaction, and device logs without changing the clinical disposition.
S142: The Biomedical Engineer evaluates a suspected mechanical or sensor fault and advises whether the affected equipment can safely return to service.
S143: The IT Operations Specialist investigates software or connectivity faults and records the technical findings for the responsible operational team.
S144: A serious or time-critical exception is escalated immediately by the observing staff member rather than held for routine review.
S145: If the clinical review remains inconclusive, the transaction stays on hold and the Clinical Pharmacist seeks a higher-level clinical decision.
S146: The final disposition records who reviewed the exception, what evidence supported the decision, and whether the medication was released, corrected, or withheld.
S147: Morrowglass validates each medication order for patient, product, dose, route, and timing fields before making it available for downstream processing.
S148: Copperfield confirms that the reconciliation queue has no unresolved discrepancy before authorizing routine cabinet replenishment.
S149: Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot uses the Order Reconciliation Snapshot to compare requested quantities with completed dispense events and current cabinet balances.
S150: Reconciliation compares the active order record with dispensing and cabinet records using a stable order identifier.
S151: The comparison preserves the order context needed to distinguish a new request from a correction or a repeat submission.
S152: Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot retains the patient, medication, dose, route, and timing details associated with each order while preparing a dispense transaction.
S153: It also checks whether the order is active and whether its authorization remains valid at the time of processing.
S154: A cancelled order is excluded from routine preparation even when a matching dispense request remains in a local queue.
S155: A corrected order is treated as a new authoritative version, and superseded values are not carried forward.
S156: Duplicate submissions are flagged for review rather than converted into additional cabinet quantity.
S157: Partial dispensing is reconciled against the quantity already recorded so that remaining quantity is calculated conservatively.
S158: Time stamps and transaction identifiers are retained to support comparison across records that arrive at different times.
S159: When the records disagree on patient, medication, or quantity, the affected transaction remains on hold until the discrepancy is resolved.
S160: The reconciliation outcome records the matched values, unresolved differences, and disposition for subsequent audit.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
